full_judgment:
2. The facts, in short, are that the respondents as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 229 of 2004 in the Court of 5th Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chittagong for declaration of title in the suit land stating, inter-alia, that the suit land situated in Touzi No. 874, under Mouza Bakoria was owned by Abdul Ahmed son of Anwar Ali and while he was in possession R.S. Survey started in 1928 and completed in 1932. In the R.S. record 4 annas and 7 pai land as 1/3 of 16 annas was recorded in the name of the grandfather of the plaintiff and the rest was recorded in the name of Mosharaff Ali and others. During that time the grandfather of the plaintiffs possessed the suit land and their names were in the R.S. record in respect of 1.93 acres of land in R.S. dag No. 1980. The grandfather of the plaintiffs used to stay in Rengaon of Burma for service and he came home and died in 1954. The grandfather of the plaintiffs left behind 2 sons namely Saleh Ahmed Chowdhury and Hafez Ahmed Chowdhury who resided outside Chittagong because of their service. The suit land measuring an area of 1.41 acres was recorded in the name of Saleh Ahmed and Hafez Ahmed in P.S. Khatian Nos.2316/9038 in P.S. dag No. 12244 and they owned and possessed the same. Saleh Ahmed Chowdhury died in 1969 leaving 3 sons Abdullah Faruk Chowdhury, died in 1969 leaving 3 sons Abdullah Faruk Chowdhury, Nasrullah Chowdhury, Golam Mohiuddin Akbar Chowdhury and 5 daughters namely Nargis Fatema, Hasina Begum, Sultana Pervin, Bilkis Fatema, Shirin Sultana as his heirs. Hafez Ahmed died in 1973 leaving behind wife Akter Banu 6 sons nainely Akter Hafiz, Anwar Hafiz, lqbal Hafiz, Ali Hafiz, Ehsan Hafiz, Mahbub Hafiz and 2 daughters Kaniz Rashul and Sayeeda Shamsi and as heirs of the deceased owned and possessed the suit land. The R.S. record was published in the name of the plaintiff but during devastating cyclone of the year 1998 their field parcha, khatian dakhilas etc. were lost. The defendant No. 1 was a stranger in the 1.43 acres of land of the suit land and his name was wrongly recorded in the khatians, On 20.05.2004 the plaintiff No. 2 while working in the suit land the defendant Nos.11 and 2 threatened them saying that they are the owner and possessor of the suit land and the plaintiffs names were not exclusively recorded in the khatians. 

 3. On 11.05.200 the plaintiff No. 2 went to the Tahsil Office for paying rent but the tahsilder refused to take rent from the plaintiff No. 2 in respect of land not recorded in the  B.S. Khatian in their names and then he came to know that the name of defendant Nos. 1/2 were recorded in the B.S. Khatian. Then the plaintiff after obtaining the certified copy of the B.S. Khatian on 21.05.2004 filed the suit for declaration of title and also for a declaration that 16 annas share of the suit land ought to have been recorded in the name of the plaintiffs. 

 4. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit through his constituted attorney and filed a written statement and the case of the defendant No. 1, in short, is that the suit is not maintainable, barred by limitation etc. and liable to be dismissed because of I insufficient court fees. The suit land of R.S. dag Nos.1980 and 1979 belonged to Khalilur Rahman, Abdul Hamid and Mosharaff Ali in their 1/3 shares of each; and R.S. record was rightly recorded in their names. Khalilur Rahman and Abdul Hamid got the share of Mosharaff Ali and these defendants are the heirs of the said Khalilur Rahman. The name of Khalilur Rahman was rightly recorded in the R.S. khatian but in the column of Comment' wrongly the name of Abdul Hamid was recorded. The P.S. khatian was also prepared wrongly according to R.S. Khatian. But in the B.S. khatian the said mistake was corrected. The defendants have been owning and possessing the suit land by regular payment of rent etc. The claim of the plaintiff of wrong record in the B.S. Khatian is not correct and the same was very much within their knowledge. They have never paid rent. The plaintiffs are not in sole possession of the suit land and they and their predecessor never claimed so. The plaintiffs instituted the suit with an ill motive just to deprive the defendant from the suit land who owned the same by inheritance and the suit is liable to be dismissed.
